transplant.notes: Inferred from the table's own footnote convention: rows for transplanted crops (e.g. Brinjal) are marked with an asterisk ('* denotes time from transplanting', p3) and the Okra row carries no asterisk, implying it is measured from direct sowing. This is an inference from table formatting, not an explicit standalone statement that okra is direct-sown.

daysToHarvestRange.notes: Corroborated by Starke Ayres' Clemson Spineless cultivar, independently stated as 50-60 days to maturity, an exact match to the KZN DARD figure.

rowSpacingRangeCm.notes: Mpumalanga provincial dept gives three grower-chosen row x in-row combinations (45x45, 50x30, 60x15 cm). Two independent ARC-VOPI okra breeding trials used different, wider row spacing for research plots: 85 cm rows x 40 cm in-row (Roodeplaat, Gauteng, rain-fed, 2015-16 seasons; Gerrano, IntechOpen 2018, https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/57756) and 100 cm rows x 30 cm in-row (Loskop, Limpopo, rain-fed, 2020-21 seasons; Gerrano et al., J. Underutilised Crops Res. 2024(1):a8, https://doi.org/10.4102/jucr.v3i1.8) — these are research-trial spacings, not grower recommendations, so are recorded here as corroboration only and not folded into the range.

yield.conditions: ARC-VOPI breeding trial, 24 okra accessions, Loskop Research Station, Limpopo province, rain-fed, 2020 and 2021 cropping seasons

evidence.quote: The okra accessions displayed a significant difference in grain yield, ranging between 60 kg/ha (Acc No. 1859.2.3.1) and 400 kg/ha (Acc No. 1214.3.1.2). The overall mean for grain yield of the genotypes was 120 kg/ha.
evidence.doc: Gerrano AS, Matjeke BM, Khoza L, et al. Phenotypic plasticity of okra for yield and associated traits. Journal of Underutilised Crops Research. 2024;3(1), a8 (open access, AOSIS)

yield.notes: This is DRY GRAIN (seed) yield from an ARC breeding trial, not the fresh-pod (vegetable) yield that is okra's normal harvested product for the farmer catalog — no South African fresh-pod t/ha figure was found in any source checked (KZN DARD's Expected Yields table has no okra row; no DAFF/DALRRD brochure exists per prior search). Recorded as the best-available SA figure with the product/conditions clearly flagged, per the honesty rule, rather than presenting it as a pod yield.

varieties.name: Clemson Spineless
varieties.notes: Described as a moderately ribbed okra with medium-green, straight, spineless pods, recommended for spring and summer planting. Supplier markets it as a general home-garden variety and does not attribute it to a specific South African province or growing zone.

gaps: SowMonths for all four rain patterns remain unsourced. KZN DARD's own sowing-calendar table (Table 6, 'Plant Establishment') has no Okra row at all. No DAFF/DALRRD production brochure for okra could be found (confirmed absent from the Wayback CDX listing of the entire 'Brochures_and_Production_Guidelines' directory). The Mpumalanga 'Indigenous Vegetables' guide and two ARC-VOPI trial papers checked in this pass all describe okra's warm-season/frost-sensitive requirement (optimum 21-29°C / min 18°C soil temp per KZN DARD's own Climatic Requirements table; ARC trials run 'during the summer growing season' / '2020 and 2021 cropping seasons' under rain-fed conditions) but none states an actual sowing month or window, so no month numbers are recorded rather than inferring them from temperature tolerance alone.

The yield figure now recorded is DRY GRAIN (seed) yield from an ARC breeding trial (60-400 kg/ha, mean 120 kg/ha) — very low, and not the fresh-pod yield that matters for the vegetable harvest; no South African fresh-pod t/ha figure was found anywhere (KZN DARD's Expected Yields table has no okra row; no DAFF/DALRRD brochure exists).

A South Africa-hosted, peer-reviewed paper on drip-irrigated okra was found on scielo.org.za (Water SA journal, vol. 49 no. 2, 2023, DOI 10.17159/wsa/2023.v49.i2.3990), but on reading its full text it describes an Indian field trial (Haryana Agricultural University, sown in India's June/Kharif season) with no connection to South African growing conditions or calendar. It was deliberately excluded as a source for okra spacing or sowMonths.

Row/in-row spacing is now sourced from a Mpumalanga provincial dept guide (grower recommendation) plus two ARC-VOPI research-trial spacings (recorded as corroboration only, not merged into the range, since trial-plot spacing is not the same as an agronomic recommendation).
Only one variety (Clemson Spineless, a general home-garden cultivar) could be verified with a specific maturity figure; no SA commercial/zone-specific okra cultivar guidance was found.
summary: Frost tenderness, days-to-harvest and ECOCROP limits are sourced from KZN DARD's Vegetable Production series and corroborated by Starke Ayres. Spacing, sow depth and seed rate are now sourced from a Mpumalanga Dept of Agriculture indigenous-vegetables guide, and yield from an ARC-VOPI okra breeding trial (dry grain, 60-400 kg/ha) — but that yield is for grain, not the fresh pods okra is actually grown for, and sowMonths remain wholly unsourced despite a dedicated search of ARC-VOPI, Limpopo/Mpumalanga dept guides, DAFF/DALRRD Wayback listings and SA peer-reviewed trials, so verdict stays partial.
